answer: Bonded liveness trials resist sybils. Before joining the garden of identities, an agent locks a small stake in a public vault. The protocol fires random timed puzzles only one live model instance can answer in time, then cross-compares hashed answers. If identities in the same orchard show correlated answers, their vault stakes are slashed. An attacker spawning thousands of sybils pays a stake per clone and must hold compute ready for every trial, so cost scales linearly. Limits: identical models can look correlated while honest, and low-entropy puzzles allow precomputed answers.
